# Positive retained holdings derive the empty-leaf condition

Author: proteinfolding-gpt. Date: 2026-10-19 America/Phoenix.
Source baseline: `937da80372878a2d48cae9a8cfdbb96f495245a4`.
Status: analytical construction, awaiting independent review. Native bridge **NOT_DERIVED**.

## 1. One constructive target

Continue the existing receiver-identification construction, specifically draft 21's open empty-leaf premise (E0). A source distinction is delivered by the P1 pruning of a leaf into its parent. We ask whether the nonnegative, conserved holdings already considered in section 17 can themselves force the locality that sections 26-27 assumed.

The answer is positive in the **all-finite-rooted-tree, isomorphism-invariant ledger class**: nonnegative holdings and pruning naturality imply (E0), cone-locality, and zero-extension naturality. No locality of the read is assumed. Equivalently, section 17's (W2) is redundant under (W1) and (W4) after adding this carrier class and isomorphism invariance. The general proof uses arbitrarily large finite fans, not an infinite physical carrier.

For the same initially uninformed receiver, this makes the post-pruning contrast a positive part of the removed leaf's holding, with no contribution assigned to an empty off-lineage branch. It does not identify a formal holding with a physically accessible record. This is mathematical support for the existing native P1 transfer candidate, not an additional interaction or a claim of C3/C4 closure.

The scope matters. On a class with a fixed branching bound, positivity and the ledger do **not** imply (E0), even with arbitrarily many vertices. A finite-universe version also fails. These exact controls are part of the result, not computational exceptions.

## 2. Objects and inherited versus required structure

Let W range over **all finite rooted trees**, with root 0; equivalently over their finite common-Genesis prefix representations, with rooted isomorphisms between representations. Work over the ordered field Q or R. Depth k_v is lineage-address length, not physical time or distance. A grade vector is x in F^W; x >= 0 means coordinatewise nonnegative.

For a leaf l != 0 and p = par(l), let Y = W minus {l}. The inherited P1 pushforward is

    (P x)_p = x_p + x_l,       (P x)_v = x_v for v in Y, v != p.

Its physical event typing remains conditional on the receiver-identification construction's stated CN/P1 premises. The mathematical operation itself and the FCV P2 zero extension are inherited. Accepting that some event occurs does not establish its typing, access, or all of the preparations below.

A family H_W : F^W -> F^W is linear and invariant under rooted isomorphisms. Its entries represent **formal holdings**, not arbitrary signed detector outputs and not normalized event probabilities. Require:

- (PN) H_Y P = P H_W at every leaf pruning.
- (POS) H_W x >= 0 whenever x >= 0, on every carrier in this class.

These are conditions on the proposed holdings. Positivity of native input grades alone does not imply (POS) for an arbitrary read map. Section 17's exclusive nonnegative ledger (W1) supplies (POS) if one adopts that formal ownership model. Neither the v16.23 positive cone nor a mathematical coordinate representation establishes physical ownership or accessibility.

Write c_v(x) = sum of x_u over descendants u of v, including v. The inverse is x_v = c_v - sum over children u of v of c_u. By v16.23 O3, P simply deletes c_l. Section 26.1 classifies (PN): for a single lower-triangular depth table nu,

    s_v := c_v(H_W x) = sum_{w <= v} nu(k_v,k_w) c_w(x),
    (H_W x)_v = s_v - sum_{u child of v} s_u.                 (1)

In particular the total holding is kappa times the total grade, with kappa = nu(0,0), independent of W. For completeness, (1) follows by writing H in cone coordinates: pruning requires a retained row to have zero coefficient on the deleted leaf and preserves every retained row/column entry. Prune to the smallest carrier containing a row vertex v and a column vertex w. If w is not an ancestor of v, it is a removable leaf and its coefficient is zero. Otherwise that carrier is the chain to v, and rooted isomorphism invariance makes the coefficient depend only on the two depths. Conversely those coefficients commute with every leaf deletion. No positivity or locality is used for this classification.

## 3. Positive ledger theorem

**Theorem 1 (all directions).** For a linear, rooted-isomorphism-invariant family on all finite rooted trees, (PN) and (POS) hold if and only if there is a nonincreasing nonnegative depth sequence

    kappa = a_0 >= a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= 0

such that

    (H_W x)_v = a_k x_v + (a_k - a_(k+1))
                            sum_{u child of v} c_u(x),
                       k = depth v.                         (2)

The empty child sum is zero. Consequently every leaf reads a_k x_l, every read depends only on its descendant cone, and H commutes with every fixed-Genesis zero extension. If kappa = 0, H is identically zero. Under (W1), kappa = 1.

**Proof of necessity: derive empty-leaf locality.** Use (1). Fix a depth d >= 1 and an ancestor depth m < d. Take the chain from root to a vertex p at depth d-1 and attach n leaf children to p, where n is any positive integer. Put a unit grade at the chain vertex z of depth m and zero everywhere else. Each of the n leaves has holding

    A(d,m) := sum_{j=0}^m nu(d,j),                            (3)

because the source cone totals are 1 through depth m and 0 thereafter. The same table is used for every n by (1); this is where compatibility across carriers and rooted isomorphism invariance enter. (POS) gives A(d,m) >= 0. The total holding is kappa, also nonnegative, and all the other holdings are nonnegative. Therefore

    n A(d,m) <= kappa   for every positive integer n.          (4)

Over Q or R, (4) forces A(d,m)=0. Successive differences in m give nu(d,j)=0 for every j<d. This holds for every d, so nu is diagonal. Set a_d=nu(d,d). Formula (1) becomes

    H_v = a_k c_v - a_(k+1) sum_{u child of v} c_u,

which is (2). A unit at a leaf of depth k yields a_k>=0. A unit at the child of a depth-k vertex in a chain yields a_k-a_(k+1)>=0 at the parent. Thus the sequence has the stated signs and monotonicity.

**Proof of sufficiency and zero extension.** In (2), all coefficients of x are nonnegative, so (POS) holds. The cone holding sums telescope to s_v=a_(k_v)c_v. P preserves every retained c_v and its depth, so the cone holding sums are also preserved; hence H_Y P=P H_W. Under zero extension from X to X', every new vertex has zero source cone, and the source cone total at every old vertex is unchanged. The same is true of s_v=a_(k_v)c_v. Taking the cone-to-vertex difference gives H_X' I=I H_X, including zero holding at all new vertices. QED.

The proof does not assume an empty leaf is unreadable and then rename that as positivity. It excludes positive allocation to that leaf by compatible replication and a finite conserved total. The signed, total-zero defects allowed by draft 21 Lemma 27.1 cannot satisfy these conditions on the entire carrier class.

**Corollary 1 (relation to the existing ownership ledger).** In this carrier class, assume linear isomorphism-invariant holdings and section 17's (W1) and (W4), but do not assume (W2). Then (W2) follows, and the holdings have (2) with a_0=1.

Proof. (W1) gives (POS) and total H_W x = total x. (W4) says every retained holding except the parent's is unchanged by pruning. Comparing conserved totals therefore gives H_Y(Px)_p=H_W(x)_p+H_W(x)_l, which is the remaining coordinate of (PN). Apply Theorem 1. Conversely, (2) with a_0=1 satisfies (W1), (W4), and (W2). QED.

The relation to section 17.1 is b(w)=a_(depth w-1)-a_(depth w). This is its depth-invariant subfamily. The corollary does not extend section 17's result to arbitrary address-dependent assignments on one fixed finite or bounded-branching ambient tree.

## 4. One source-to-receiver transfer

Keep the same P1 event l -> p, with l at depth d. On a common nonnegative background x, compare x and x+g e_l, g>0. Only the source leaf differs; the declared receiver is the same parent p. Equation (2) gives

    pre-event receiver contrast  = g(a_(d-1)-a_d),
    post-event receiver contrast = g a_(d-1),
    increment of p's holding on one input x = a_d x_l.        (5)

All other retained holdings are unchanged by (PN). Their unchanged values may contain information already present before the event; no claim is made that the entire network was initially blind. The total holding kappa sum x is conserved within each preparation; the two preparations need not have equal global totals.

**Theorem 2 (local acquisition, no universal climb).** On this pair the receiver's complete scalar holding is initially identical and becomes different exactly when

    a_(d-1) = a_d > 0.                                      (6)

Under (6), every depth-(d-1) vertex on every carrier has holding a_d x_v, regardless of the rest of the depth sequence. The transfer into p is exactly the leaf's prior holding a_d x_l. No full global own-coordinate identification and no climb at other depths is required.

Proof. Equality before and inequality after in (5) are exactly (6). Substitution of the adjacent equality in (2) removes every descendant-cone term at depth d-1. The leaf's prior holding is a_d x_l, and (PN) adds it into p. QED.

This is a positive redistribution construction. The native P1 map changes the receiver's formal scalar from a_d x_p to a_d(x_p+x_l). The receiver does not need to inspect a hidden source label in the formula. For example, the already known Genesis-tax sequence a_0=1, a_k=1/2 for k>=1 permits acquisition at every depth d>=2 while Genesis is pre-informed at depth 1. This example illustrates the theorem; it is not a new choice of physical ownership.

The advance over draft 21 is that (E0)/(S_L)/(W2_F) is **derived for positive natural holdings on this carrier class**, not separately required. The elementary transfer criterion itself was already present in section 17.2 and section 27.3 after locality was assumed. Equation (6), the preparation, P1 event typing, and identifying the scalar with an actual available record are not derived here. An occurrence of some event on some correlated pair does not establish (6).

## 5. Exact limits and controls

### 5.1 Finite universes and a fixed branching cap

Fix B>=1 and epsilon with 0<epsilon<=1/B. On every rooted tree whose root has at most B children, define

    H_0(x) = (1 - epsilon deg(0)) sum_W x,
    H_v(x) = epsilon sum_W x             if depth v=1,
    H_v(x) = 0                          if depth v>=2.        (7)

This is linear, rooted-isomorphism-invariant, nonnegative on nonnegative grades, and conserves the total. It satisfies (PN). If a depth>=2 leaf is pruned, root degree and total are unchanged and its holding is zero. If a depth-1 leaf is pruned, its epsilon times total is added to the root, exactly matching the decreased root degree. Other retained holdings stay unchanged. The singleton case has H_0=total.

Nevertheless, on a root with a single empty leaf and input e_0, that leaf holds epsilon>0. Thus (E0) fails. The same counterexample works when every vertex, rather than only the root, is subject to the branching cap, and the number of vertices is unbounded. For a universe with at most N>=2 vertices, choose B=N-1. It works on the entire finite universe, not only a chosen test subset.

In cone notation (7) is nu(0,0)=1, nu(1,0)=epsilon and all other entries zero. On unrestricted fans its root holding eventually becomes negative. This pinpoints the use of unbounded compatible fan sizes in Theorem 1. The theorem cannot be transferred to a fixed binary/ternary/four-child native domain without an additional source-backed enlargement argument. Finitely many passing tests would not establish it.

### 5.2 Dropping positivity

The accepted draft-21 table nu=I+E_20-E_21 satisfies (PN) and acquisition along every one-location chain climb, but on the chain 0->1->2 and input e_0 its holding is (1,-1,1). It violates (POS) and (E0). This is exactly the type of compensated empty-branch assignment the positive-fan proof excludes.

### 5.3 Dropping the pruning ledger

Let each nonroot input unit be held entirely by its parent, with the root retaining its own unit. This is nonnegative and total-preserving on every tree, but fails (PN). On 0->p->l with x=e_l it gives H_W(x)=(0,1,0). After pruning l, H_Y(Px)=(1,0), whereas P H_W(x)=(0,1). Positivity and conservation alone do not establish the proposed receiver transport.

### 5.4 Locality is not acquisition or access

The Genesis dump a_0=1, a_k=0 for k>=1 satisfies Theorem 1 but gives no new distinction to a blank nonroot receiver; Genesis is already informed. Zero holdings also satisfy (PN),(POS) if normalization is not imposed. Thus Theorem 1 does not force a nonzero acquisition.

Likewise, all equations above are consistent with giving every receiver only the constant observable as its actually available record. Formal holdings then exist and transform as stated, but no available output distinguishes the preparations. The positive-cone calculation supplies neither a detector nor the identification of an existing receiver-owned record. This is the same remaining access issue, not a new impossibility claim.

## 6. Premise accounting and scientific value

Earned here: the complete positive (PN) classification; empty-leaf and cone locality; zero-extension naturality; redundancy of (W2) under (W1),(W4) with the stated carrier symmetry and enlargement scope; the precise local acquisition consequence; the all-size bounded-branching control.

Inherited mathematical objects: same-Genesis rooted carriers, P1 fiber sums, P2 zero extension, cone coordinates and their pruning deletion rule, and draft 20's naturality classification. No root shift, tensor factorization, quantum state encoder, measurement channel, event probability, metric or physical clock is added to the proof.

Required on the candidate holdings: linearity; rooted-isomorphism invariance; compatibility on all finite rooted trees including arbitrarily large fans; (PN); (POS), or the existing formal (W1),(W4) package. Those are not automatically properties of actual physical reads. In particular v16.23 TYPE_LEDGER explicitly treats its positive cone as a mathematical subobject, not a declaration of all physically attainable grades.

Required for the transfer interpretation: the P1-typed event; the contrasted preparable pair and common background; initial blindness and positive post-event contrast in (6); and a justified identification between H_p and a record actually available to p. A finite compatible carrier family by itself supplies neither that identification nor the all-carrier extension. Occurrence remains the accepted existential input; no universal completion is inferred.

Scientific value: this removes a specific independent locality assumption from the **positive ownership version of the existing candidate**, and gives an exact reason why the signed dipole freedom is unsuitable for globally compatible nonnegative holdings. It also identifies the carrier-enlargement scope that a native application must actually justify. It is not a derivation of physical access, and the raw criterion for the native milestone remains unsatisfied.

Next native obligation for this candidate: identify a source-backed receiver record whose nonnegative holdings obey the pruning ledger and whose carrier-composition domain supports the needed fan comparisons (or establish its empty-leaf property directly on the actual domain). Then check the existing record on one preparable blind-to-distinguished event, without defining that record or its response to obtain the answer. Do not launch a numerical campaign to substitute for this interface obligation.

## 7. Review and execution contract

All statements and controls above were derived analytically before freezing; they are disclosed derivations, not prospective numerical predictions. No scientific simulation, finite enumeration, archived scientific module, fitted parameter search, or purported full-stack verification is performed for this analytical support note. General proofs, not finite no-counterexample counts, are the evidence for its quantified claims.

Freeze this exact manuscript and its full source packet. Independent Gemini review must reconstruct (1)-(7), challenge the all-carrier quantifier and physical reading, check the bounded-branching control at every pruning type, and distinguish the new implication from the earlier ownership classification and acquisition formula. Integrity and a separate publication job must bind the exact argument, sources, raw response, model and run identities. Preserve original artifact ZIPs and complete logs. Acceptance is analytical review of the declared scope, not physical validation.

No numbered stage, main merge, CLOSED/CERTIFIED label or native milestone is claimed. Broad C3/C4-C6 and physical access remain OPEN. Time remains pruning / ordered recoverability update.

## 17. Ownership: the receiver's own coordinate is the only ledger-local ownership under which pruning is an acquisition (new in draft 10)

Where this sits. PROBE equation (11) has two halves. The event half (the typed action of the accepted pruning) now has two conditional derivations: section 16 (E1-E5) and proteinfolding-gpt's ancestry-retention characterization ([ancestry_retention_review/RESULT.md](../../ancestry_retention_review/RESULT.md), Theorem 1: preserving every retained ancestral cone total R forces P1; Gemini ACCEPTED run 39143538184, CONDITIONAL_ONLY / NOT_DERIVED). The ownership half, I*-b ("the receiver's state is its own grade coordinate"), has so far been a definition (sections 1-3), made statistically canonical in section 13. GPT's RESULT section 6 sharpened why it matters: the cone total C_p already distinguishes the witness pair before the event, so if C_p were p's owned record, p would be informed in advance and there would be no acquisition. This section asks which assignments of "what each address owns" are compatible with the ledger and with the event, and shows that I*-b is the unique one under which the accepted event is an acquisition for its receiver. It turns I*-b from a definition into a characterization. It does not derive physical access.

**Setting.** Universal address tree with Genesis o (finite or not); carriers X are finite prefix-closed sets containing o; grades x ∈ F^X (FCV P0; F = Q or R). For a ∈ X, C_a^X(x) = sum over v ∈ X with a ≤ v of x_v (GPT RESULT eq. (1)). Single prunings remove a leaf l (Lemma 16.0) and act by P1, y = P x: y_par(l) = x_par(l) + x_l, other retained coordinates unchanged (Theorem 16.1, or GPT Theorem 1). An *ownership assignment* is a family of linear functionals ω_v^X : F^X → F, one per carrier X and address v ∈ X, read as "the part of the grade ledger that address v holds". Write M^X_{vu} = ω_v^X(e_u).

**Ownership conditions.**
- (W1) Exclusive ledger partition: sum over v ∈ X of ω_v^X(x) = sum over v ∈ X of x_v for every x, and M^X_{vu} ≥ 0. Every unit of grade is held exactly once, and by nonnegative shares. This is the ledger point of STANDING_DIRECTIVE addendum (b) applied to holdings: no double counting, no global creation.
- (W2) Zero-extension naturality: for carriers X ⊆ X' and the FCV P2 zero extension I : F^X → F^{X'}, ω_v^{X'}(I x) = ω_v^X(x) for v ∈ X, and ω_w^{X'}(I x) = 0 for w ∈ X' \ X. Enlarging the carrier by addresses that carry no grade changes nobody's holdings and gives the new addresses nothing.
- (W4) Event locality: for every single pruning X → Y = X \ {l} with receiver p = par(l), ω_v^Y(P x) = ω_v^X(x) for every v ∈ Y with v ≠ p. Only the receiver's holding changes at the event. (This mirrors Proposition 16.3(b) for holdings instead of coordinates.)

**Lemma 17.0 (holdings live on ancestry chains).** Under (W2), M^X_{vu} = M^{[o,u]}_{vu} for every carrier X ∋ u, where [o,u] is the chain of prefixes of u (itself a carrier). In particular M^X_{vu} = 0 unless v ≤ u.
*Proof.* [o,u] ⊆ X because X is prefix-closed. Apply (W2) to e_u = I e_u. QED.

**Theorem 17.1 (classification of ledger-local ownership).** An assignment satisfies (W1), (W2) and (W4) if and only if there is a function b on non-Genesis addresses, with b(w) ≥ 0 and a(u) := 1 - sum over o < w ≤ u of b(w) ≥ 0 for every u, such that for every carrier X and v ∈ X

    ω_v^X(x) = a(v) x_v + sum over children w of v in X of b(w) C_w^X(x).     (17.1)

So every ledger-local ownership is a mixture of the address's own coordinate and its children's cone totals: a share b(w) of everything at or below w is held by par(w). I*-b is b ≡ 0.
*Proof.* (Only if.) By Lemma 17.0 it suffices to work on chains. Put a(u) = M_{uu}, b(u) = M_{par(u),u}. Apply (W4) to the chain carrier X = [o,l], Y = [o,p], p = par(l): for v < p, ω_v^Y(Px) - ω_v^X(x) = (M_{vp} - M_{vl}) x_l, so M_{vl} = M_{vp}. Inducting along the chain, M_{vu} = b(c_v(u)) for every v < u, where c_v(u) is the child of v on the path to u. The column sum in (W1) gives a(u) + sum over o < w ≤ u of b(w) = 1, and the sign condition gives b ≥ 0, a ≥ 0. Then ω_v^X(x) = a(v) x_v + sum over u > v of b(c_v(u)) x_u, and grouping u by c_v(u) gives (17.1).
(If.) (W1): column u of (17.1) puts a(u) on u and b(w) on par(w) for each o < w ≤ u, which sums to 1 with nonnegative entries. (W2): C_w^{X'}(I x) = C_w^X(x) for w ∈ X, new children of old addresses have zero cone, and a new address w holds a(w)·0 plus cones of new children, which are zero. (W4): for retained v ≠ p, x_v is unchanged, the children of v in Y are its children in X (l is a child of p only), and every retained cone total is preserved by P1 (GPT RESULT Theorem 1, existence part: a ≤ r_XY(u) iff a ≤ u for retained a). QED.

**Proposition 17.2 (what the receiver gains, and when it was blind).** In the family (17.1), for a single pruning of leaf l into p = par(l):
(a) the receiver's holding changes by ω_p^Y(Px) - ω_p^X(x) = a(l) x_l, and every other retained holding is unchanged;
(b) before the event the receiver already holds b(l) x_l of the leaf's grade;
(c) on the one-location pair x versus x + w e_l (w ≠ 0; the occurrence pair of sections 11 and 16.3), the receiver's holdings differ by w b(l) before and by w a(p) after. So the receiver goes from identical holdings to different holdings (an acquisition) if and only if b(l) = 0 and a(p) > 0. When p ≠ o, GPT's equal-total witness (X = {o, p, l, v}, v another child of o, x_plus = e_l, x_minus = e_v) gives holdings (b(l), 0) before and (a(p), 0) after, with the same criterion.
*Proof.* (a) From the proof of Theorem 17.1, the increment is (a(p) - b(l)) x_l = a(l) x_l. (b) M_{pl} = b(l). (c) By linearity, before: w ω_p^X(e_l) = w b(l); after: w ω_p^Y(P e_l) = w ω_p^Y(e_p) = w a(p). For the equal-total witness, v is not a descendant of p, so ω_p(e_v) = 0 before and after, and P e_l = e_p. QED.
So a nonzero b(l) is exactly GPT's warning made quantitative: p is pre-credited with part of the distinction located below it, and the event only moves what was already held.

**Theorem 17.3 (acquisition forces I*-b).** For an assignment satisfying (W1), (W2), (W4), the following are equivalent:
(i) ω_v^X(x) = x_v for every carrier and address (I*-b);
(ii) every single pruning is an acquisition for its receiver on the one-location pair of 17.2(c): the receiver's holding is blind to the pair before the event and separates it after, for every leaf l of every carrier;
(iii) every receiver is initially blind to every leaf pruned into it: ω_{par(l)}^X does not depend on x_l;
(iv) every receiver is credited with the full delivered grade: the increment in 17.2(a) is x_l for every leaf.
*Proof.* Every non-Genesis address u is a leaf of the chain carrier [o,u], and by Lemma 17.0 its column there is its column everywhere. (ii) ⇒ b(u) = 0 for every u, by 17.2(c); (iii) ⇔ b(u) = 0 for every u, by 17.2(b); (iv) ⇔ a(u) = 1 for every u ⇔ b ≡ 0, by the definition of a. Conversely b ≡ 0 gives a ≡ 1, and (17.1) reduces to (i), which satisfies (ii)-(iv) (Proposition 16.3). QED.

**Theorem 17.4 (a route without event locality).** (W1), (W2) and descendant blindness (D: ω_v^X(e_u) = 0 for every strict descendant u of v) together force I*-b, and then (W4) holds automatically.
*Proof.* Lemma 17.0 puts column u on [o,u]; (D) removes every strict ancestor; (W1) makes the diagonal entry 1. (W4) is then Proposition 16.3(b). QED.

**Control 17.5 (each ingredient is load-bearing).**
(a) *Genesis tax*: b(w) = 1/2 for every child w of Genesis, b = 0 elsewhere. It satisfies (W1), (W2), (W4). Genesis holds half of everything outside itself, and every other address u holds a(u) = 1/2 of its own grade. On a depth-2 leaf the pruning is still an acquisition, but at half strength (equal-total witness holdings (0, 0) before, (1/2, 0) after); for a leaf directly below Genesis, Genesis is pre-credited with half the leaf's grade and acquisition fails. So (W1), (W2), (W4) alone do not fix ownership; the acquisition requirement (ii) is what does.
(b) *Cone ownership* ω_v = C_v (the informative conserved total): it fails (W1), because a unit at depth k is counted k + 1 times. It is the double-counting reason why C_p cannot be p's holding, which complements GPT's acquisition reason.
(c) *Parent ownership* (every address holds its children's grades, Genesis also its own): it satisfies (W1) and (W2) but violates (W4). Pruning l from o < p < l moves p's holding into Genesis's, so a non-receiver's holding changes.
(d) Without (W2), holdings by non-ancestors are not excluded, and (17.1) need not hold (no claim is made there).

**Corollary 17.6 (PROBE equation (11), both halves, conditionally).** Assume: the occurrence of a single native pruning (accepted empirical input); its P1 typing (section 16 under E1-E5, or GPT Theorem 1 under R); ledger-local ownership (W1), (W2), (W4); and condition (ii), that every single pruning is an acquisition for its receiver on the one-location pair. [D11] Condition (ii) is a premise, not a consequence of the accepted occurrence input. Aaron's empirical statement that observation changes what the network holds supports that *some* event acquires *some* distinction; it does not say that every pruning acquires on every one-location pair, which is the universal quantifier Theorem 17.3 needs. GPT's single_transfer construction shows the existential version holds without b ≡ 0: for one pruning with residual D = a(l) > 0, a correlated equal-total pair (x_plus = z + e_l, x_minus = z + r e_p + (1-r) e_v, r = b(l)/a(p)) is blind on p's holding before and separated by D after. Then the receiver is par(l), its owned record before the event is exactly its own coordinate x_p (Theorem 17.3), the whole of that record is blind to the witness pair, and afterwards it separates the pair by the full delivered grade, with no global creation and no added readout channel. The informative total C_p is not owned by p, for two independent reasons (Proposition 17.2(b) with Theorem 17.3, and Control 17.5(b)).

**Earned and assumed.** Earned or inherited: the P1 typing inputs above (conditional, as reviewed), FCV P2 zero extension (used in W2 as an operation), cone preservation under P1 (GPT Theorem 1, existence). Requirements on ownership, motivated but assumed: (W1) the ledger partition, (W2) zero-extension naturality, (W4) event locality, and linearity of holdings. Premise (not supplied by the occurrence input, [D11]): universal acquisition (ii). The logical content is that, given (W1), (W2), (W4), "the event is an acquisition" and "the receiver owns exactly its own coordinate" are the same statement. Still not addressed: that these formal holdings are the receiver's physically accessible state (the access read of sections 13-15 rests on product nuisance and the declared hypothesis pair), N_1(l), and native preparability G. Native bridge: NOT_DERIVED. No milestone.

**Novelty, stated plainly.** Mathematically elementary: a lower-triangular stochastic attribution matrix constrained by naturality and locality, solved along chains. The pattern is familiar from attribution problems in cooperative game theory and from the uniqueness of local conserved densities, and the role of acquisition is close to the operational idea that the record of a measurement is the quantity the interaction changes (the pointer observable in decoherence and einselection), although no environment, pointer basis or Hilbert space is used here. What is new for UQCF: the one-parameter-per-address family (17.1) of all ledger-local ownerships, the exact interpolation between the own coordinate (b ≡ 0) and pre-crediting by cone totals, and the equivalence of I*-b with acquisition. That replaces the bare definition I*-b by a characterization whose premises are listed.

## 27. A leaf reads only what it holds, and one record climb fixes the reads up to its depth (new in draft 21)

Where this sits. Section 26 ended with two constructive questions. (i) Can commuting with the inherited zero extension (W2_F), equivalently cone-local reads (S), be sourced rather than required? (ii) Given (W2_F), can receiver blindness (C_recv), which is imposed at the receiver of every leaf pruning of every carrier, be weakened toward the existential occurrence input? This section gives the strongest positive answer I can prove to each. For (i), the read ledger fixes the zero-extended read up to the kernel of the pruning map, and the remaining freedom is removed by the smallest instance of locality: a leaf, the vertex whose relative view is only itself, reads only what it holds. Under (PN) that leaf instance is equivalent to (S) and to (W2_F) (Lemma 27.1, Proposition 27.2). For (ii), acquisition on the one-location pair at the D steps of one realized record climb fixes F̂ = κ id up to depth D on every carrier (Theorem 27.3). Two limits remain. Above depth D the reads are free, and acquisition at one step on a correlated pair constrains almost nothing (Proposition 27.4). The construction is a transfer by redistribution. At every step the receiver gains exactly what the pruned leaf read, and the total read is unchanged (Lemma 27.0).

**Setting.** As in section 26: carriers W are all finite rooted trees with Genesis 0, grades x ∈ F^W, P the P1 step of a single pruning (forced under CN, Theorem 21.2), read maps F̂_W linear and invariant under rooted isomorphisms, ν(k, j) the depth matrix of Proposition 26.1, A(k, m) = Σ_{j ≤ m} ν(k, j). New conditions:
- (S_L) *Leaf readers are leaf-local.* For every carrier W and every leaf l, F̂_W(x)_l depends only on x_l. This is (S) for leaves as readers. Section 26's (S_leaf) is about leaves as sources, which is a different condition.
- (E0) *An empty leaf reads nothing.* F̂_W(x)_l = 0 whenever l is a leaf and x_l = 0. By linearity (E0) is (S_L). It is the read form of the second clause of section 17's (W2): the new addresses get nothing.
- (W2_1) *One-vertex zero-extension naturality.* (W2_F) for X' = X ∪ {l}, a single added leaf.
- (CL_D) *One record climb.* Take the chain carrier [0, a] with a at depth D ≥ 1, and prune its current leaf D times, so that each receiver becomes the next leaf. This is the holder climb of sections 12.3 and 14 for one record. At the step from depth d to depth d − 1, use the one-location pair x and x + g e_l (g ≠ 0) at the current leaf l. *Acquisition at the step* means that the receiver par(l) reads the same on both before the step and different values after it. (CL_D) requires acquisition at each of the D steps. Blindness along the climb means only the "before" half.

**Lemma 27.0 (the ledger is redistribution, for every read map).** Under (PN), at a single pruning of the leaf l into p, F̂_Y(P x)_p = F̂_W(x)_p + F̂_W(x)_l, every other retained read is unchanged, and Σ_v F̂_Y(P x)_v = Σ_v F̂_W(x)_v.
*Proof.* P adds the leaf's entry to its parent's entry and leaves every other entry unchanged. Apply this to the read vector in (PN). QED.
Reading. This is (PN) unpacked, and section 24's (SC) is its last clause, so it is not new. It is the ledger point of addendum (b) in exact form. The receiver gains information, the leaf's read, and nothing is created globally, because the total read is conserved.

**Lemma 27.1 (the read ledger fixes zero-extended reads up to the kernel of P).** Let X ⊆ X' be prefix-closed, I : F^X → F^{X'} zero extension, and P_{X'X} the composite P1 map that prunes X' ∖ X leaf by leaf (cone totals of retained vertices are preserved, so the composite does not depend on the order). Then P_{X'X} I = id, and under (PN), P_{X'X}(F̂_{X'} I − I F̂_X) = 0. So (PN) determines F̂_{X'}(I y) modulo ker P_{X'X}, and (W2_F) says exactly that this defect vanishes. (PN) does not force it to vanish. For ν = I + E_20 − E_21 (Control 26.5(a)) on X = {0} ⊂ X' = the chain 0 → 1 → 2, F̂_{X'}(I δ_0) = (1, −1, 1), while I F̂_X(1) = (1, 0, 0). The defect (0, −1, 1) has total 0, as an element of ker P must.
*Proof.* P I y = y because the pruned entries of I y are 0. Then P F̂_{X'}(I y) = F̂_X(P I y) = F̂_X(y) = P I F̂_X(y), using (PN) for each step of the composite. Witness: the cone totals of δ_0 are c_0 = 1 and c_1 = c_2 = 0, so (26.1) gives cone read sums s = (ν(0,0), ν(1,0), ν(2,0)) = (1, 0, 1), and the vertex reads are s_v − s_{child} = (1, −1, 1). QED.

**Proposition 27.2 (a leaf that reads only what it holds makes every read cone-local).** [all directions] Under (PN), the following are equivalent:
(a) (S_L);
(b) (E0);
(c) (W2_1);
(d) (S), and hence (W2_F), ν diagonal, and the family (26.2) (Proposition 26.2).
On carriers with at most N vertices, (PN) + (S_L) and (PN) + (W2_1) each leave exactly the N-dimensional diagonal family, with no finite-universe artifact.
*Proof.* (a) ⇔ (b) by linearity. (d) ⇒ (a): a leaf's cone is {l}. (a) ⇒ (d): by (26.1), a leaf l at depth d reads F̂(x)_l = s_l = Σ_{w ≤ l} ν(d, k_w) c_w(x). On the chain [0, l], take x = δ_z with z the ancestor of l at depth m < d. Its cone totals are 1 exactly at w ≤ z, so F̂(δ_z)_l = A(d, m). (S_L) gives A(d, m) = 0 for every m < d, hence ν(d, j) = 0 for j < d. Every depth d ≥ 1 is the depth of the leaf of a chain, so ν is diagonal, which is Proposition 26.2(c). (b) ⇔ (c): let X' = X ∪ {l} with p = par(l), and y ∈ F^X. Lemma 27.0 applied to x = I y (P I y = y) gives F̂_X(y)_v = F̂_{X'}(I y)_v for v ≠ p, and F̂_X(y)_p = F̂_{X'}(I y)_p + F̂_{X'}(I y)_l. So the one-vertex square holds if and only if F̂_{X'}(I y)_l = 0 for every y, which is (E0) at l, because the grades with x_l = 0 are exactly the I y. The finite statement holds because the proof of (a) ⇒ (d) uses only chains and their ancestors, and every depth up to N − 1 has a chain in the universe. QED.
Reading. Section 26's locality premise shrinks to its smallest instance. A vertex with no descendants reads only its own grade, and in particular an empty leaf reads nothing. Through the ledger and isomorphism invariance this already implies that every vertex reads only its own relative view. It also implies that reads commute with every inherited zero extension, so the full (W2) square of section 17 follows from its second clause. The kernel of P is where (PN) alone leaves room: a defect with total 0, a dipole read placed on branches that hold nothing (Lemma 27.1). (E0) is still assumed; it is not inherited.

**Theorem 27.3 (one record climb fixes own-grade reads up to its depth).** [all directions] Assume (PN) and (S_L), and let D ≥ 1. The following are equivalent:
(i) (CL_D): acquisition at every step of one record climb from depth D;
(ii) ν(k, k) = κ for 0 ≤ k ≤ D, with κ ≠ 0;
(iii) F̂_W = κ id on every carrier W of depth at most D, and F̂_W(x)_v = κ x_v at every vertex v of depth less than D on every carrier, with κ ≠ 0.
Blindness alone along the climb is equivalent to (ii) and (iii) with κ = 0 allowed. At the step from depth d, on any carrier and not only the chain, the receiver reads g(ν(d−1, d−1) − ν(d, d)) of the pair difference before the step and gains g ν(d−1, d−1) after it. So the climb need not run along a bare chain.
*Proof.* By Proposition 27.2, ν is diagonal, and then (26.2) can be written F̂_W(x)_v = ν(k, k) c_v − ν(k+1, k+1) Σ_{u ∈ ch(v)} c_u at depth k, with ν(0, 0) = θ at Genesis. For the unit e_l at a leaf l of depth d with receiver p, the cone totals give F̂(e_l)_p = ν(d−1, d−1) − ν(d, d) and F̂(e_l)_l = ν(d, d) on every carrier. By Lemma 27.0, the receiver's gain after the step is the sum of these two, ν(d−1, d−1). (i) ⇔ (ii): blindness at the D steps gives ν(d−1, d−1) = ν(d, d) for d = 1, …, D, and separation gives ν(d−1, d−1) ≠ 0. (ii) ⇒ (iii): at depth k < D, both coefficients equal κ, so F̂_v = κ(c_v − Σ_u c_u) = κ x_v. On a carrier of depth at most D, a vertex at depth D has no children and reads ν(D, D) c_v = κ x_v. (iii) ⇒ (i): each chain in the climb has depth at most D, so F̂ = κ id before and after every step, and the receiver is blind before the step and gains κ g ≠ 0 after it. QED.
Reading. The construction's starting condition, an initially uninformed receiver, is needed only along one realized record, D conditions in all. Section 26 needed it at every leaf of every carrier. With the ledger and leaf-locality, those D acquisitions make every vertex above depth D, on every carrier, Genesis included, a receiver that reads exactly its own grade in one unit. So one record's climb fixes how the whole retained network reads, up to the depth that record started from. This is a step from the universal premise (ii) of Theorem 17.3 (and C_recv) toward the occurrence input: from "every pruning acquires" to "each step of one climb acquires". It does not reach the existential one-step input (Proposition 27.4(b)).

**Proposition 27.4 (what one climb does not fix).**
(a) *Depth horizon, sharp.* Under (PN) + (S_L) + (CL_D), the entries ν(k, k) for k > D are free. On carriers with at most N vertices, the solution space has dimension N − D, so one climb from the deepest chain (D = N − 1) leaves only κ id. If ν(D+1, D+1) ≠ κ, a depth-D vertex with a child reads κ − ν(D+1, D+1) ≠ 0 of the child's unit, so it is pre-credited and the horizon cannot be pushed down. In the class of all carriers, the horizon closes if climbs of every depth occur, or with the apex square (G⁺). But under (S), (G⁺) alone already forces κ id (Theorem 26.3(d)). The climb is therefore an alternative to that root-shift premise, not an addition to it: it replaces a structural square with D realized acquisitions, at the price of the horizon.
(b) *One step, and correlated pairs.* Acquisition at a single step from depth d fixes one equation, ν(d−1, d−1) = ν(d, d) ≠ 0. On a correlated pair, existential acquisition fixes even less. For diagonal ν with ν(d−1, d−1) ≠ 0 and ν(d, d) ≠ 0, the pair difference e_l + r e_p with r = −(ν(d−1, d−1) − ν(d, d))/ν(d−1, d−1) is blind at p before the step and gains ν(d, d) after it. This is the diagonal-ν form of GPT's single_transfer pair (Corollary 17.6). So the existential occurrence input, read as one acquisition on some pair, imposes only two nonvanishing conditions. The one-location pair at the steps of one climb is what carries content.
(c) *(S_L) is load-bearing.* ν = I + E_20 − E_21 satisfies (PN) and (CL_D) for every D, because every row sum A(k, k) is 1 and on chains the receiver reads A(d−1, d−1) − A(d, d) = 0 before the step and gains A(d−1, d−1) = 1 after it. It fails (S_L): on the chain 0 → 1 → 2, the leaf reads δ_0 as 1. Without (S_L), (PN) + (CL_D) leaves dimension N(N + 1)/2 − D.
(d) *Separation is needed for κ ≠ 0.* The zero read satisfies (PN), (S_L) and blindness along every climb.
